claims.text: Built once per document rather than once per link, and sorted at build time so two processes see candidates in the same order
claims.why: The function sorts the known_files and builds dictionaries; sorting ensures deterministic order.

claims.text: A bare note name is Obsidian's 'shortest path when possible': it names a file anywhere in the vault. Two files with that basename is exactly the tie this module refuses to break.
claims.why: When '/' not in name, _hits returns set from by_base lookup, which returns all basename matches; caller (resolve_wiki_target) returns WIKI_AMBIGUOUS if len(hits)>1.

claims.text: A path is read BOTH as vault-root-relative (what Obsidian does) and as document-relative (what a reader who knows markdown assumes). When the two readings name two different files that BOTH exist, the link is genuinely ambiguous and gets counted as such
claims.why: The function builds candidates list: one with stripped leading '/' (root-relative), and if not starting with '/', also a document-relative candidate by joining with document's dirname. Both are looked up in by_path.

claims.text: default_ext is appended ONLY as a second round, when the name as written matches nothing: [[Note]] finds Note.md, while ![[chart.png]] still finds the png rather than hunting for chart.png.md.
claims.why: The function first tries raw, then if default_ext is non-empty and raw doesn't end with default_ext, appends ext and tries again. So raw .png is tried first, then extension not appended if already ends with .png.

claims.text: The per-occurrence view: a reader UI needs to chip an individual link as unresolved or ambiguous, and an aggregate count cannot tell it which one.
claims.why: The function returns a list of (link, target, status) for each wikilink, preserving per-link granularity.

claims.text: A document linking to itself is not an edge
claims.why: The function checks if target == parse.document and appends (link, None, WIKI_RESOLVED) without adding to edges.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT folded into internal_links: that function is the contract index.py builds document_links from today, and doc->code is a different relation from doc->doc. Mixing them would have made the wiki's first feature a silent change to an existing edge set.
claims.why: The claim refers to index.py and existing edge sets not present in this chunk.

claims.text: doc_targets is a superset of internal_links' first return value: same standard-markdown edges, plus the wikilink ones.
claims.why: The function calls internal_links which is defined by signature only; its actual return value is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: A section runs to the next heading of EQUAL OR HIGHER level, so an H2 contains its H3s -- the same containment a Python function has over its nested defs (_units_from_tree emits both).
claims.why: In the loop, end is set to the index of the next heading with level <= current level, so sections span until a heading of equal or higher level.

claims.text: (resolved rel targets, unresolved count). Sorted, de-duplicated, self excluded -- a document linking to itself is not an edge.
claims.why: The function adds to resolved set (de-duplicated), excludes self via 'target != parse.document', and returns sorted list.

claims.text: distilled False means the raw document was returned because no skeleton of it was SMALLER than the document itself (a short README, a doc that is nothing but headings). Returning the raw text there is the honest outcome: the alternative is a 'distillation' that grows the prompt, which this repo has already measured as a lie and pinned with a test.
claims.why: The logic for setting distilled is not in this chunk; only the dataclass definition is present.
